page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2gne.16xlarge is a storage-focused virtual instance belonging to the Local SSDs family. Built on the KVM hypervisor and utilizing x86_64 architecture, this instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processors operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system provides 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 256.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

A primary hardware component of the instance is its dense bundled storage, consisting of 7679 GB of integrated local solid-state drives. For connectivity, the configuration provides a baseline network throughput of 20 Gbps. It does not include hardware GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, focusing physical host resources strictly on compute cores, memory capacity, and high-capacity local disk operations.

The bundled local SSD capacity renders the ecs.i2gne.16xlarge an economical configuration for IOPS-demanding scenarios compared to provisioning equivalent network-attached block volumes. A notable operational tradeoff involves the ephemeral nature typically associated with direct-attached local storage, which necessitates robust application-level replication strategies. The instance is suited for relational database clusters, distributed NoSQL datastores, real-time log analytics engines, and data pipeline staging environments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2gne.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance configured with 64 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 vCPUs clocked at 2.5 GHz and 256.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Designed for high-throughput transactional and disk-intensive deployments, the server bundles 7679 GB of high-speed local solid-state drive storage along with a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps. The architecture lacks GPU accelerators, dedicating host allocations toward compute and direct-attached storage performance. By bundling extensive local SSD space, the instance delivers high resource density for IO-heavy workloads without relying on external network block storage. Given the absence of hardware persistence guarantees common to local media, operational resilience relies on application-tier redundancy. This configuration serves workloads including large distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, search indexing engines, batch ETL jobs, and data warehousing tasks.
